diagnosis: Gastric hyperplastic polyp with high-grade dyspalasia
legend: Gastric hyperplastic polyp with high-grade dysplasia. Note dramatic hyperplasia of the foveolar component with background intestinal metaplasia and zones of abrupt transitions to high-grade dysplasia. Patient had several large polyps resulting in gastric outlet obstruction followed by distal gastrectomy, and a history of undergoing H. pylori eradication treatment few months prior to the procedure.

Characteristic features of gastric hyperplastic polyps include irregularly shaped, haphazardly dilated foveolae in a background of loose oedematous stroma, with variable numbers of inflammatory cells. The surface is frequently eroded.

The polyp contains oedematous lamina propria and numerous thin-walled vessels in the mucosa. The surface epithelial cells contain variable amounts of mucin; some are mucin-depleted whereas others harbour large cytoplasmic vacuoles.
Distended goblet cell–like mucinous cells in hyperplastic foveolae are called globoid cells.

A Mucosal prolapse polyp, a subtype of gastric hyperplastic polyp, found in the pyloric channel, shows mucosal hyperplasia in combination with cytoplasmic depletion of the foveolar epithelium. A few bundles of smooth muscle cells emanate from the muscularis mucosae into the polyp.
B Polypoid foveolar hyperplasia, a subtype of hyperplastic polyp, is characterized by elongated pits with minimal oedema in the lamina propria.

A subtype of gastric hyperplastic polyp near the gastrojejunal anastomosis, showing marked atrophy (i.e. antralization) of the oxyntic glands with foveolar hyperplasia, mucosal oedema, and mucosal cysts.
A polypoid lesion near the gastroduodenal anastomosis contains cysts extending from the deep mucosa into the submucosa.

A large gastric hyperplastic polyp is composed of oedematous mucosal projections lined by regenerative epithelial cells. Surface erosions and cystically dilated glands are present. Aggregates of thin-walled vessels expand the mucosa in an area of erosion.

Low-grade dysplasia on the surface of a polyp; note the tall columnar cells containing elongated nuclei located at the base; foveolar-type and goblet cells are seen in a hybrid manner; hyperplastic foveolar cells are also seen.
High-grade dysplasia in a polyp, containing enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei with readily apparent mitotic figures and a loss of cell polarity.
